title: 'Quem novit': a cipher letter to Christian IV, 20 July [1627 or 1628] (Rigsarkivet, TKUA Nederlandene B.41, unit 261377, image 443; with catalogue 2541): code broken, read in part

steps.what: Sweep of TKUA Nederlandene B.41 (unit 261377) images 426-475 by plain download; image 443 right page found to hold a sign cipher signed 'Quem novit', no decipherment beside it.

Reader 1 (the breaker) transcribed the page line by line from 2x crops; frozen 02:18:36 UTC, md5 836d644f. Disclosure: the letter values took shape while transcribing, so 'frozen before decoding' means before any scripted decode, not before any guess.

The clear text continues '... lasset E. unverhalten sein', so the first two cipher words were taken as 'Gnadigster Konig'; the rest of the key followed from word patterns, by hand. 23 signs with a value, one (n) without.

dec_B.py run once on the frozen text: 93 of 103 units S (90.29%), 0 of 5,000 shuffled keys and 0 of 5,000 random-value keys as good (German 4-grams). Filed on #450 with this figure; the figure is now withdrawn as the headline (see below).
Held-out: with only the key signs seen in lines 01-10, 65 of 66 cipher words of lines 11-19 decode in full (63/68 S). Not blind: the key was not fitted on 01-10 alone.

Prior art: CLEAR in what was checked, thin (anonymous letter). Writer proposed as Christian Wilhelm of Brandenburg, Administrator of Magdeburg, at Venice in July 1627 (one article, read through a summariser): derived, not proved.

Reader 2, blind (b129; key and reading not seen before freezing at 09:49:43 UTC): sign agreement with reader 1 511/565 (90.44%); under the key 62 of 104 units S (59.62%), 0 of 5,000 shuffled keys. 13 of its E units differ from reader 1 only by the g/q or pi/Z sign class.

Reader 3, blind (b137; frozen 11:22:40 UTC with its own sign chart, mapped to the key by shape before decoding): sign agreement with reader 1 497/564 (88.12%), with reader 2 484/564 (85.82%); 49 of 110 units S (44.55%), 0 of 5,000. Two of its shape mappings were wrong (its Z is reader 1's S; its n is reader 1's Z or P).

Adjudication for this folder: each reader-1 sign takes the value at least two of three readers give (frozen 13:17:09 UTC, decoded once 13:17:19 UTC): 70 of 103 units S (67.96%); all three agreeing: 47 of 103 (45.63%). 0 of 5,000 shuffled keys for every reading, seeds 20261112 and 7. The filed 90.29% is withdrawn as the headline; the key stands.
German reading and English translation from the adjudicated decode, 33 holes marked in place (13 g/q class, 7 one-sign emendations, 4 pi/Z/n, 3 c/e, 3 codes, 3 other signs).

Integration check (R4): independent decoder from key_B.txt and reader 1's transcription reproduces the decode; 100 cipher words, 60 are words of a German vocabulary built from the repository's German corpora (len 3+), 0 of 3,000 shuffled keys reach 60 (best 6). adjudicated.tsv decoded with my own code: 88 units decode fully, 70 equal a form in s_forms.txt = 70/103. Image 443 and 447 fetched from the archive API and compared; the g/q tail distinction could not be settled at this resolution.

Correction by the contributor (PR #588) after Mark Vladimir Prizmic's comment on issue #450 and his preprint (doi:10.5281/zenodo.24210516): images 465-466 of the same unit hold a second letter in this hand and key, dated in cipher 25 July 1627, found and read by Prizmic. The sweep of images 426-475 had reported no sibling in this key; that was wrong. The gloss of code 118 as the place of writing (Venice likely) is withdrawn: 118 stands in the dating line of both letters, written at different places.

Integration check of PR #588: images 465 and 466 (api.rigsarkivet.dk/ao/v1/images/48900949 and 48900950, 4473 x 3436) fetched and looked at. Same hand and sign repertoire as image 443; closing page signed 'Quem novit E.'. key_B.txt unchanged reads the opening 'gnedigster konig', then 'in den siebenden tagk' and 'wegen', and the dating line '.118. den 25 iulii an[no] tausendt 6 c. undt zwantzigk sieben' (about 12 cipher words read by eye; the body was not transcribed). In the number word the sign n, which has no value in key_B, stands twice where 'zwantzigk' needs z, so n = z is supported on the image; key_B.txt is left as stamped and no count for image 443 changes. The second letter is Prizmic's reading and is not added to this folder. A further independent key for the same letters was reported on the issue by Brice Dudout (16 of 16 shared letter values equal to key_B, value z proposed for the sign without a value); no files were sent, so it is recorded as reported, not checked.

outcome.method_basis: Crib 'Gnadigster Konig' for the first two cipher words, guessed from the clear continuation ('... lasset E. unverhalten sein') and the addressee's rank, then word patterns, by hand. No decipherment of this letter exists.
outcome.fraction_read_source: decryptions/adjudicated.txt and counts.txt: 70 of 103 cipher units (reader 1's division) decode to a German word as written when each sign takes the value at least two of the three readers give; the three codes, reader 1's seven emendations and every unit with a disputed sign are counted not read. Reader figures beside it: 93/103 (reader 1, withdrawn as headline), 62/104 and 49/110 (blind readers).

validation.notes: The contributor's own shuffled-key control (0 of 5,000 shuffled keys reach the score of any of the four readings, seeds 20261112 and 7; checks/shuffle_control.out); docs/_validate.py was not run on this letter. Integration control: 60 of 100 cipher words in a German word list for the true key, best of 3,000 shuffled keys 6.

credits.note: 'Quem novit' letter: key from the ciphertext with a crib, read in part, with three readings by separate AI sessions; issue #450
three transcriptions of image 443 (one by the breaker, two blind) by separate AI sessions

found and read the sibling letter of 25 July 1627 at images 465-466 of the same unit (same hand, same key), which corrects the sibling sweep and the gloss of code 118 as the place of writing; issue #450 comment of 14 Nov 2026

gaps.detail: Three tokens here. 118 also stands in the dating line of the sibling letter of 25 July 1627 (images 465-466: '.118. den 25 iulii', seen on the image 14 Nov 2026), which reports an arrival after a voyage and so was written at another place: 118 is a word of the dating formula, not the place of writing (corrected 14 Nov 2026 after M. V. Prizmic, issue #450). Neither letter gives it a value. The chancery sheet at image 447 is for another code.

gaps.item: g/q sign class (13 units) and pi/Z/n, c/e classes (7 units) disputed between readers
gaps.detail: The tails of g and q cannot be separated at the resolution available here (image 443, 4473 x 3436); a person comparing them at full size is needed.

texts.label: 'Quem novit' to Christian IV, 20 July [1627 or 1628]
texts.summary: The writer (H.) tells the King he has waited into a third week for a galley, at cost and to his vexation; small galleys were there but nobody, [117] least of all, would advise risking them; the Signoria has now assigned a large one, which came yesterday, and he leaves today. He has borrowed another 3,000 thalers and asks the King to have them paid, to be deducted later. [117] has resolved nothing on his proposal, but he hopes W. will declare themselves better. Context: the Signoria and the galleys point to Venice (not proved), in the Thirty Years' War; the writer is not identified. The code 118 stands in the dating line and is not the place of writing. A sibling letter of 25 July 1627 (images 465-466, read by Mark Vladimir Prizmic) points to 1627.

reading_review.by: an AI model, for Malcolm McBratney: a model reading, not a person, and not independent (the session that prepared these files). A person's review is still owed.
reading_review.note: Read as sentences against the translation. Connected German whose sense can be followed; 33 holes marked in place.

texts.note: read_share is the adjudicated strict share 70/103 = 67.96%.

outcome.notes: The filed figure (93/103 = 90.29%, reader 1 alone) is withdrawn as the headline because two blind readers did not reproduce it (59.62%, 44.55%). Repository scripts (docs/_check_reading.py, docs/_validate.py, docs/_check_profile.py) were not run; checks verified by hand.

prior.where: None found in what was checked (b97 and b126, 12 Nov 2026): Danske Magazin, Kong Christian IV's egenhaendige Breve, Danske Samlinger, Historisk Tidsskrift, Swedish Handlingar, DECODE, Cryptiana, archive.org full text ('Quem novit', the Administrator of Magdeburg at Venice). Thin: an anonymous letter cannot be searched by name; Christian Wilhelm's 1627 correspondence and Venetian state papers not checked. 'Not printed' cannot be proved.

human: Malcolm McBratney directed the work, set the rules (every attempt recorded, transcriptions frozen before decoding, blind second and third transcriptions by separate sessions, shuffled-key controls, no claim without its check) and sent the result; Claude sessions found the letter, transcribed, built the key, read and checked. No reading by a person without AI.
